profile.lede: I am Fahad a Computer Engineer who builds reliable software that continues to perform efficiently long after launch day.

paragraphs.t: My core focus bridges the gap between Computer Engineering and
: I design and develop backend architecture using Django and PostgreSQL, build frontend systems with React, and manage the infrastructure that keeps these systems running
The true quality of any software is proven after its release. Leveraging my engineering background, I focus on building
—maintainable, clearly structured, and engineered around real-world constraints from the very first commit.
Most of my work sits at the intersection of
, and frontend engineering—solving problems that span the entire stack from a comprehensive engineering perspective.

items.description: At Flint Consulting, I develop and maintain production-ready full-stack web applications using Django and React. My role involves designing scalable REST APIs, implementing secure authentication systems, and architecting database structures with PostgreSQL and MySQL. I also manage the Linux VPS infrastructure—configuring Nginx, Gunicorn, domain mapping, and SSL certificates—while overseeing production deployments and maintaining secure hosting environments with robust backup strategies.

During my internship as a Computer Engineer at Emara Hail, I developed a real-time data acquisition system and contributed to the design and implementation of UI/UX interfaces. I focused on troubleshooting complex issues at the intersection of hardware and software, while systematically documenting all engineering solutions and technical workflows.

I managed operational reporting and handled large-scale datasets, ensuring high levels of data integrity. By leveraging advanced Excel and Google Sheets functions, I maintained accurate figures and dependable reports to support seamless business operations.

projects.title: Projects
projects.subtitle: A deep dive into the systems I've engineered from backend architecture to live production deployments.

items.title: AARC
items.subtitle: Four role-specific workspaces operating on one recruitment and rental-management backend.

overview.t: AARC is a production-grade recruitment platform coordinating the full operational workflow across
four independent dashboards

: Employees, External Offices, Administration, and Rental Administration. A shared Django REST Framework backend centralizes authentication, records, and workflow transitions, while each React-based dashboard exposes only the specific actions and tools relevant to its role.

architecture.frontend: React dashboards featuring role-aware navigation, dynamic forms, and operational queues, connected via a unified API client
architecture.backend: Django REST Framework handling core authentication, complex permission policies, workflow endpoints, and administrative services
architecture.database: MySQL relational database optimized for user management, recruitment records, rental operations, and state tracking
architecture.deployment: Linux VPS infrastructure utilizing Nginx as a reverse proxy and Gunicorn to serve the Django application

highlights: Four tailored dashboards for Employees, External Offices, Administrators, and Rental Managers
Centralized authentication with granular, role-based authorization enforced at the API level
Automated recruitment workflows that move through controlled operational states rather than disconnected manual updates
Full production stack hosted and operated on a self-managed Linux VPS
challenges: Enabling four dashboards to share a single backend without leaking records or actions between roles
Maintaining workflow consistency when multiple teams interact with the same recruitment process
Ensuring high availability for React and Django services on a self-managed production server
solutions: Implemented reusable DRF permission policies and scoped every database query to the authenticated user's role
Modeled recruitment stages as validated backend state transitions to prevent invalid workflow actions
Orchestrated static delivery, reverse proxying, and application serving through a robust Nginx and Gunicorn configuration

items.title: Shahm Law
items.subtitle: A law-firm website backed by a custom publishing, request, and communication system.

overview.t: Shahm Law combines a professional legal-services interface with a
purpose-built Content Management System (CMS)

. The central administration dashboard manages site content, team access, newsletter subscribers, and email campaigns, alongside contact enquiries, service requests, and internal notifications within a single, organized workspace.

architecture.frontend: Public-facing service pages and a secure administration dashboard for content management and communication tracking
architecture.backend: Custom CMS and application services for structured publishing, role-based access control, newsletter management, and automated request processing
architecture.database: A relational model linking pages, subscribers, enquiries, service requests, users, and notifications for seamless data flow
architecture.deployment: Production deployment at shamlaw.sa with integrated automated email-delivery workflows

highlights: Structured content publishing allowing editors to update the site without code modifications
End-to-end management of newsletter subscriptions and outbound campaigns within the admin system
Streamlined operational queues that separate general enquiries from specific legal service requests
Granular role management limiting publishing and communication capabilities to authorized personnel
challenges: Combining editorial workflows and client-service operations without creating a cluttered dashboard
Managing large-scale newsletter delivery while preventing duplicate campaigns
Keeping public forms accessible while protecting sensitive administrative workflows
solutions: Separated content, subscribers, and requests into focused modules sharing a unified access model
Built campaign and recipient state-tracking into the workflow to ensure reliable and verifiable delivery
Validated public submissions through dedicated endpoints and exposed them only to authorized roles

items.title: KneeGuide
items.subtitle: A clinical rehabilitation platform for tracking patient exercise progress and recovery over time.

overview.t: KneeGuide is an active rehabilitation-technology research project I helped build, born out of hackathon collaboration with further competitions planned. It is currently
pursuing intellectual property protection
, so its technical architecture and implementation are intentionally not detailed here — this listing reflects the project's real progress and my contribution to it, not a full technical writeup.

items.title: TripSplit
items.subtitle: A shared trip ledger for joining groups, recording expenses, and tracking the remaining budget.

overview.t: TripSplit provides travel groups with a single, unified financial record. A trip owner creates the workspace and distributes a simple
invite code
; members join the same ledger to record expenses and view real-time updates on spending and the remaining budget, eliminating the need for separate or manual calculations.

architecture.frontend: A responsive web interface for trip creation, code-based joining, member management, and real-time budget summaries
architecture.backend: Application services that enforce trip membership, validate invite codes, manage expense ownership, and perform accurate budget calculations
architecture.database: A relational ledger connecting trips, members, invite codes, and expense entries to ensure data synchronization across all users

highlights: Short invite codes allowing travelers to join the correct trip seamlessly without manual coordination
Every recorded expense is linked to the shared trip and the specific member who entered it for full transparency
Real-time remaining budget derived from a single authoritative ledger visible to all members
Membership management for trip owners while participants maintain the ability to record costs
challenges: Preventing invite codes from granting unauthorized access to unrelated trips
Keeping financial totals consistent when multiple members add or revise expenses simultaneously
Representing membership and expense ownership without duplicating trip data per user
solutions: Implemented server-side validation and resolution of codes before establishing scoped membership
Derived budget summaries from authoritative database records rather than relying on client-side calculations
Modeled trips, memberships, and expenses as separate entities so a single ledger serves every participant efficiently

items.title: Dorina Pro
items.subtitle: A browser-based football tournament engine supporting league and knockout competition formats.

overview.t: Dorina Pro manages football tournaments entirely within the browser environment. Organizers can select between league or knockout modes, enter teams and match results, and the application automatically derives
standings, qualifiers, winners, and the final top three rankings
from the tournament state persisted in LocalStorage.

architecture.frontend: A single-page application (SPA) featuring independent logic flows for league standings and knockout bracket calculations
architecture.backend: None; all tournament rules, logic, and progression are executed client-side in the browser
architecture.database: Utilizes LocalStorage for persistent storage of teams, fixtures, results, standings, and overall tournament progress
architecture.deployment: Static frontend deployment hosted at dorina.fyaa.io

highlights: Instant recalculation of league tables and points as match results are updated
Automated advancement logic that moves winners through knockout rounds seamlessly
Persistent tournament state that survives page refreshes without requiring user accounts or remote databases
Comprehensive completion logic to announce the champion and final top-three positions
challenges: Supporting both league and knockout formats without mixing incompatible data progression models
Reconstructing a valid and consistent tournament state after a browser refresh
Handling result edits without leaving stale standings or incorrect winners
solutions: Isolated each competition mode behind deterministic calculation functions to ensure logical integrity
Serialized minimal core data and recomputed all derived views (like standings) upon page load
Treated standings and advancement as derived data, triggering a full recalculation after every modification to maintain consistency

items.title: Student Results
items.subtitle: A lightweight result lookup tool that reads synchronized student records directly from Google Sheets.

overview.t: Student Results eliminates the need for a custom application server by leveraging
Google Sheets as the primary data source
. This solution allows staff to continue updating familiar spreadsheets while providing students with a focused frontend to search synchronized records using their identifying information.

architecture.frontend: A streamlined search interface that validates student input, queries the published dataset, and presents matching records
architecture.backend: No custom backend required; Google Sheets serves as the managed record source
architecture.database: Google Sheets rows containing synchronized student result records, updated in real-time
architecture.deployment: Static frontend deployment hosted at alkeysaei.fyaa.io

highlights: Staff can update results through their existing spreadsheet workflow without needing complex data-entry interfaces
The system reads synchronized records without the overhead of a separately maintained API server
Secured access that narrows results based on specific student identifying information
Minimal operational overhead and maintenance due to the simplified deployment architecture
challenges: Using a spreadsheet as a live data source while ensuring predictable and accurate lookup behavior
Handling inconsistent data entry in cells, such as varying spaces, casing, or formats
Avoiding unnecessary infrastructure for a narrowly scoped read-only workflow
solutions: Implemented a read-only data flow, treating the spreadsheet as the single authoritative source of truth
Integrated a normalization layer to sanitize values before comparing search fields with sheet data
Utilized a static client architecture that operates independently of a custom application server

items.title: Terhal (Tourism Cooperative Association)
items.subtitle: A bilingual, multi-page website showcasing the association's initiatives and tourism programs.

overview.t: Terhal is a comprehensive digital platform built with React, spanning over ten pages in both Arabic and English. The site effectively organizes the association's identity and tourism programs into a shared
bilingual system
that dynamically adapts navigation, reading direction (RTL/LTR), and responsive layouts across both languages.

architecture.frontend: An advanced React component system shared across more than ten pages, ensuring design consistency and ease of updates
architecture.backend: None; public information is delivered as a high-performance, frontend-only website
architecture.database: None; page content and metadata are bundled within the application for optimal speed and reliability
architecture.deployment: Production deployment on Netlify at terhalv1.netlify.app

highlights: Over ten distinct pages sharing a unified navigation system and reusable UI sections
Full Arabic language (RTL) support without the need for maintaining a separate codebase or site
Consistent information hierarchy and visual structure preserved across both languages
Fully responsive design covering everything from dense internal pages to the core landing experience
challenges: Synchronizing navigation structure and routing across two languages and multiple independent paths
Supporting both RTL and LTR layouts without duplicating code for every component
Maintaining a clear and readable content hierarchy across mobile and desktop breakpoints
solutions: Centralized route and navigation definitions to dynamically handle language switching and path resolution
Engineered direction-aware React components that automatically adjust layout rules based on the active language
Defined responsive behavior at the component level to ensure consistent presentation throughout the entire multi-page site

items.title: OQOL Professional Development Association
items.subtitle: A tailored WordPress implementation providing the team with direct and full control over digital content management.

overview.t: OQOL is a specialized WordPress implementation customized to meet the organization's specific page and publishing requirements. WordPress serves as a flexible operational layer, enabling the team to
maintain and update site content without developer intervention
while ensuring the public presentation remains strictly aligned with the approved structural framework.

architecture.frontend: Development of a customized WordPress theme and page templates specifically engineered to match the organization's content hierarchy
architecture.backend: Configured WordPress administration with tailored editing controls and optimized media management workflows
architecture.database: Utilizes the WordPress relational content store for efficient management of pages, settings, and media references
architecture.deployment: Production WordPress hosting deployed at the official domain oqol.sa

highlights: Custom templates reflecting specific content types, providing a streamlined publishing experience over generic page builders
Empowered the team to handle routine copy and media updates directly through the WordPress admin interface
Implemented reusable content patterns to maintain visual and structural consistency across repeated sections
Ensured a smooth handover by staying within familiar WordPress operations for the organization's staff
challenges: Balancing editing flexibility with a fixed, client-approved visual presentation
Preventing routine content updates from accidentally breaking the page structure or responsiveness
Keeping the administration interface simple and intuitive for non-technical editors
solutions: Mapped recurring content into constrained templates and reusable fields to prevent design drift
Limited editing choices to the specific controls necessary for each page type, ensuring structural integrity
Configured the CMS dashboard around the organization's specific publishing workflow, making management tasks straightforward

items.title: CodeDuo
items.subtitle: A corporate services website that transforms complex software capabilities into a clear and professional enquiry path.

overview.t: CodeDuo presents software development services through a responsive and modern corporate frontend. The information architecture seamlessly transitions from broad capability areas to specific service details and contact actions, utilizing
consistent branded components
to ensure a professional and cohesive user experience.

architecture.frontend: A component-based website featuring dedicated service pages, company information, and intuitive enquiry paths
architecture.backend: No application backend is required for the public presentation layer, ensuring rapid loading times and optimal performance
architecture.database: None; corporate and service-related content is bundled with the frontend for maximum stability
architecture.deployment: Production website hosted at the official domain codeduo.sa

highlights: Service categories structured around core software delivery capabilities to clearly communicate value to potential clients
Visual patterns creating continuity between the corporate overview and individual service details
Contact actions remain highly accessible and clear across both desktop and mobile layouts
Typography, spacing, and color rules implemented as reusable frontend primitives to ensure brand consistency
challenges: Explaining multiple technical service lines without creating a dense or overwhelming catalog
Maintaining a unified visual system across sections of varying sizes and functions
Preserving clear and motivating enquiry paths, especially on small mobile screens
solutions: Grouped offerings by client problems and delivery outcomes rather than providing a dry technical list
Developed shared section, typography, and spacing primitives within a centralized component system
Strategically placed responsive contact actions at deliberate decision points throughout the user journey

items.title: Wasla (Social)
items.subtitle: An open-source, bilingual link hub designed for self-hosting and full digital identity customization.

overview.t: Wasla is a powerful, self-hostable alternative to popular "link-in-bio" services like Linktree. It packages profile details, social links, bilingual content, and visual identity into a
lightweight, deployable frontend
, allowing users to own their platform without depending on external subscription-based services.

architecture.frontend: A responsive, bilingual link page with configurable profile settings, destinations, and branding
architecture.backend: No complex backend is required, focusing on deployment simplicity and high performance
architecture.database: Configuration-based content management, eliminating the need for an independent database service
architecture.deployment: A static, self-hostable build that can be deployed anywhere, with a live instance at social.fyaa.io

highlights: Delivers both Arabic and English profiles from a single, lightweight codebase
Easily update brand colors, identity, and destination links without rebuilding the core layout
Complete independence from third-party link platforms and subscription accounts
Near-zero operational costs by deploying as a static site on simple hosting services
challenges: Keeping customization approachable for users without a full administration backend
Ensuring the compact layout works naturally and attractively in both RTL and LTR orientations
Ensuring ultra-fast page loads, especially when accessed from mobile social media applications
solutions: Separated profile content and brand settings from the core presentation components for easy modification
Used direction-aware rules so a single component tree seamlessly supports both languages
Minimized the deployment footprint and removed all server-side dependencies for near-instant performance
